A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain 31 readable pages, including Appendices A-J. Full-text comparison and rendered-page checks establish matching scientific content without material gaps.

before.justification: v5 reports original model-training results, geometry-optimization outcomes, and molecular-dynamics simulations in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v6 retains these original empirical results, including accuracy measurements, optimization failure rates, and fine-tuning and multiple-time-stepping experiments.

M1.justification: The PET variants, conservative fine-tuning procedure, and hybrid multiple-time-stepping method are unchanged (Sections 4.1 and 4.8; Appendices D, H, and I).

E1.justification: Coverage is identical, including bulk water, QM9 and MPtrj geometry optimization, OC20 training, and the additional molecular and material simulation cases.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding experiments, including PET and SOAP-BPNN variants, ORB-v2, MACE-MP-0, SevenNet, and Equiformer.

E3.justification: Training splits, optimization criteria, simulation conditions, and evaluation procedures match. For example, Figure 15 retains the OC20 subset of 15,000 training and 5,000 validation samples.

E4.justification: The interaction-range sensitivity test, closed-loop work analysis, optimization failure studies, thermostat comparisons, and MTS-stride analyses are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Uncertainty reporting is identical, including temperature uncertainties and bands spanning two standard errors in Figures 12, 13, and 17. No run-count or seed information is added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and plotted findings match. Table 1, for example, retains force MAEs of 19.4 and 24.8 meV/Å for conservative and non-conservative PET trained on energies and forces.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and reasoning are unchanged, including the Jacobian-asymmetry measure in Section 3, the derivations in Appendices A-C, and the MTS integrator in Appendix I.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and Section 5 retain the same claims about non-conservative-force failures and the benefits of hybrid conservative/direct-force training and simulation.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations match, including thermostat-induced artifacts, confounding between force-field and sampling errors in Appendix G.5, and instability at large MTS strides in Appendix I.

D1.justification: Implementation descriptions, hardware and timing details, software versions, and code/data access information are identical (Appendices D and J; Software and Data section).

R1.justification: Related-work passages and the reference list are identical. No cited work or substantive relationship to prior research is added, removed, or reframed.

P1.justification: Only the page-1 arXiv stamp and its hyperlink change from v5, dated 26 July 2025, to v6, dated 25 October 2025. Prose, terminology, and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: All 18 figures and 10 tables retain their displays, captions, and placement. Rendered pages match except for the marginal version/date stamp on page 1; the document layout is unchanged.

improvement.justification: v6 only updates the arXiv version stamp and associated link. The scientific arguments, empirical evidence, limitations, reproducibility information, and presentation across the main text and appendices are unchanged, establishing no meaningful net difference in overall quality.
